item.title: The Daily Facts — October 19, 2026
item.description: The Daily Facts — Monday, October 19, 2026 Good evening, and welcome to The Daily Facts. It's Monday, October nineteenth, twenty twenty-six. I'm your host, and here's a straightforward look at the day's world news. Where details are disputed or unconfirmed, we'll say so. Ukraine We begin in Ukraine, where Russia carried out a large overnight strike on energy infrastructure from Sunday into Monday. According to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, sixteen ballistic missiles were fired at the Kyiv region, more than ten energy sites were hit, and about five hundred fifty thousand families across eleven regions were left without power. Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched two hundred sixty-nine Shahed-type drones, fifty-nine of them jet-powered, and that two hundred forty-three drones and four cruise missiles were downed. The Kyiv Independent reported three people killed and fifty-three injured over the past day. Zelenskyy said there was no early warning from partners. Russia's Defense Ministry said it struck defense industry targets and a data center in the Kyiv region. Later Monday, Reuters reported that a drone strike on a park in Nova Vodolaha, in the Kharkiv region, killed six people, including three children, and injured about fifteen. On diplomacy, Reuters, citing three sources, reports that Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are expected to travel to Norway this week for talks on Ukraine. Two of those sources said Zelenskyy is expected to attend. The plans are described as tentative. The Wall Street Journal reports that Vladimir Putin has proposed a three-way summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen on November eighteenth and nineteenth. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said there have been discussions but no agreement. President Trump has not agreed, and Ukraine's foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, voiced opposition. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking in Uzbekistan, referred to "talks of a meeting" and said there is "no pause" in intelligence sharing with Ukraine. Rubio also said Ukrainian strikes in the Black Sea hit vessels carrying US-owned oil, but that this was not deliberate. And in Lithuania, Defense Minister Kaunas said a Ukrainian drone that entered the country was diverted by Russian electronic warfare during an attack on Saint Petersburg. Ukraine apologized. Lithuanian officials said the incident is not linked to a recent Starlink arson case, and the national security commission met Monday. Middle East and Iran Turning to the Middle East. In Yemen, a Houthi missile attack on a government training camp near Ataq, in Shabwa province, has seen differing casualty figures through the day. Early on, The National and other sources said at least eighteen were dead, Reuters also said at least eighteen, AP said at least twenty, and China's Xinhua reported twenty-five. By late morning, AP and Reuters cited local authorities saying fifty-three people were killed and more than two hundred wounded. Three ballistic missiles struck the training center, and the Houthis acknowledged the attack. Officials stress the figures are preliminary. Separately, Riyadh's airport reopened Monday, according to a notice to airmen, following Houthi attacks, though Flightradar24 data showed more than eighty percent of flights cancelled. Eighteen people have died in total in those attacks, and Lufthansa has suspended service until November eighteenth. In Iran, there are two conflicting accounts of an incident at the Konarak naval base. Iran says US forces targeted the base; according to Iran's navy, two light projectiles hit a thirty-five millimeter gun and wounded two soldiers.
